#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=16| passage=The preposterous altruism '''too'''!{{...}}Resist not evil. It is an insane immolation of self—as bad intrinsically as fakirs stabbing themselves or anchorites warping their spines in caves scarcely large enough for a fair-sized dog.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-26|author=w:Leo Hickman| volume=189| issue=7| page=26| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/jul/01/how-algorithms-rule-world-nsa How algorithms rule the world]| passage=The use of algorithms in policing is one example of their increasing influence on our lives. And, as their ubiquity spreads, so '''too''' does the debate around whether we should allow ourselves to become so reliant on them – and who, if anyone, is policing their use.}}
# {{lb|en|conjunctive}} [[also|Also]], [[in addition]] {{n-g|marks a statement as equally valid as the preceding one}}.
#: {{syn|en|as well|additionally|eke<q:obsolete>}}
#: {{ux|en|There has been a cutback in federal subsidies. Rates have been increasing '''too'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|He's always willing to help. He, '''too''', is generous with his time. }}
#: {{ux|en|It is important to remember, '''too''', that she is generous with his time. Sometimes, '''too''', she does ask for the odd favor.}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=1|passage=They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had '''too'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author={{w|K. A. Applegate}}|title=The Attack|series=Animorphs|volume=26|passage=The Isk were true symbiotes. The Isk cannot live without the Yoort. And to ensure that this symbiosis would be real, the Yoort, '''too''', were modified. Now Yoort cannot live without Isk and Isk cannot live without Yoort. They are one creature with two parts.}}
# {{lb|en|degree}} To an excessive degree, more than enough {{n-g|indicates that the degree of a quality is more than what is needed or wanted}}.
#: {{syn|en|unduly|over|over-|overly|excessively}}
#: {{hypo|en|much too|far too|way too}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|extremely|unnecessarily|all too}}

#: {{ux|en|This water is '''too''' polluted for us to drink (it).}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't be '''too''' quick to blame others.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1620|section=Nouell 8, The Eighth Day|title= {{w|The Decameron|The Decameron, Containing an Hundred Pleaſant Nouels: Wittily Diſcourſed, Betweene Seuen Honourable Ladies, and Three Noble Gentlemen}}| author= w:Giovanni Bocaccio| tlr= w:John Florio| publisher=Isaac Iaggard| url= https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=FEz6_FECCI0C| passage={{...}}purſued his vnneighbourly purpoſe in ſuch ſort: that hee being the ſtronger perſwader, and ſhe (belike) '''too''' credulous in beleeuing or elſe ouer-feeble in reſiſting, from priuate imparlance, they fell to action; and continued their cloſe fight a long while together, vnſeene and vvithout ſuſpition, no doubt to their equall ioy and contentment.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21582516-worlds-thirst-oil-could-be-nearing-peak-bad-news-producers-excellent Yesterday’s fuel]| passage=The dawn of the oil age was fairly recent. Although the stuff was used to waterproof boats in the Middle East 6,000 years ago, extracting it in earnest began only in 1859 after an oil strike in Pennsylvania.{{...}}It was used to make kerosene, the main fuel for artificial lighting after overfishing led to a shortage of whale blubber. Other liquids produced in the refining process, '''too''' unstable or smoky for lamplight, were burned or dumped.}}
# {{lb|en|degree|colloquial}} To a high degree, [[very]].
#: {{syn|en|so|all that}}
#: {{ux|en|She doesn't talk '''too''' much.  I'm not '''too''' sure about this.}}
# {{lb|en|emphatic|colloquial|childish}} {{n-g|Used to contradict a negative assertion with present and simple past forms of ''be'', ''do'', and auxiliary verbs}}
#: {{syn|en|so}}
#: {{ux|en|You're not old enough yet. ― I am '''too'''!}}
#: {{ux|en|You can't jump that fence. ― Can '''too''' jump it!}}
#: {{ux|en|We haven't been mean to you. ― Have '''too''', plenty of times}}
# {{lb|en|archaic|colloquial}} {{n-g|Used for emphasis, without reference to any previous statement.}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|text=The trooper thanks his informant and rides slowly on, looking about him. {{...}} He comes to a gateway in the brick wall, looks in, and sees a great perplexity of iron lying about in every stage and in a vast variety of shapes— {{...}} "This is a place to make a man's head ache '''too'''!" says the trooper, looking about him for a counting-house.}}

====Usage notes====
* Used in the conjunctive sense, ''too'' is used [[Appendix:Glossary#postpositive|postpositive]]ly, often offset with a pause (in speaking) or commas (in writing), and pronounced with {{w|phrasal stress}}.
* When used in their senses as degree adverbs, ''[[very]]'' and ''too'' never modify verbs; ''[[very much]]'' and ''[[too much]]'' do instead.

|passage=The most common type of encoder is one that converts a '''nonbinary''' number system into an equivalent binary system.}}

* The {{w|U.S. Government Publishing Office Style Manual}} item 6.29 recommends to spell ''non-'' prefixed words without a hyphen unless an overriding consideration applies.<ref>{{R:GPOSM/CR}}</ref>

According to Kroonen (2013), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-||to stir, rise}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|rāsian||to explore, examine, research}}, {{cog|ang|rīsan||to seize, carry off}}, {{cog|ang|rǣran||to raise}}. {{doublet|en|rear}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|physical}} To cause to [[rise]]; to [[lift]] or [[elevate]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' your hand if you want to say something; to '''raise''' your walking stick to defend yourself}} #: {{ux|en|the flag was '''raised'''}} ## To form by the accumulation of materials or constituent parts; to build up; to erect. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' a wall, or a heap of stones}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|Isaiah|xxxix|3|passage=I will '''raise''' forts against thee.}} ## To cause something to come to the surface of water. ##: {{ux|en|The ship was '''raised''' ten years after it had sunk.}} ## {{lb|en|nautical}} To cause (the land or any other object) to seem higher by drawing nearer to it. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' Sandy Hook light}} ## To make (bread, etc.) light, as by [[yeast]] or [[leaven]]. ## {{lb|en|figurative}} To cause (a dead person) to live again; to [[resurrect]]. ##: {{ux|en|The magic spell '''raised''' the dead from their graves!}} ## {{lb|en|military}} To remove or break up (a blockade), either by withdrawing the ships or forces employed in enforcing it, or by driving them away or dispersing them. ## {{lb|en|military|transitive}} To relinquish (a [[siege]]), or cause this to be done. ## {{lb|en|metalworking|transitive}} To emboss (sheet metal), or to form it into cup-shaped or hollow articles, by hammering, stamping{{,}} or spinning. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To create, increase or develop. #: {{ux|en|We need to '''raise''' the motivation level in the company.}} #: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' the quality of the products; to '''raise''' the price of goods; to '''raise''' (increase) taxes}} ## To [[collect]] or [[amass]]. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' a lot of money for charity; to '''raise''' troops}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1955|month=February|author=T. B. Act, were increasingly loath to part with their cash.}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[call up]] the [[force]]s of, to raise the [[troop]]s from. ##* {{RQ:Jack Straw|III|55|May it pleaſe your Grace that I ſhall '''raiſe''' the ſtreets,

(1970-1975), and began to live in a village in Shansi in 1975.}} ## To [[promote]]. ##: {{syn|en|elevate|empower|uplift|Thesaurus:aggrandize}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' somebody to office}} ## To
